criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.

stories.notes: All 9 tabs built and reachable; every list view's cards drill down to a detail page (Outcomes uses the brief's sanctioned no-measures empty state instead, since plan.derived.measures is empty). Verified in-browser over a local static server (fetch needs http://, not file://): zero console errors across all 9 pages and their drill-downs, Sample mode shows plausible labelled data on every tab, Real mode shows the honest current state (0/13 stories, 0/41 criteria, grey "not checked from here" on Systems, "not enforced yet" on all 4 Guardrails, "no runs recorded"/"no skills registered yet" on AI Agents). Found and fixed one real bug during verification: the Users & Use Case role-matching regex only recognized an uppercase vowel, so lowercase role names like "approver" (from plan.derived.roles) fell through to "As a approver" and matched 0 stories instead of 1 — fixed to a case-insensitive test.

criteria.text: Given a token request, when it is approved, then the token is issued and enforced.
Given a revoked token, when it is used, then the action is blocked.
Trust: Every action is logged in the Audit Log.

tests_added: issueToken > issues an active token scoped and expiring as requested
issueToken > saves the issued token in the store, so it can be enforced against later
issueToken > refuses to issue a token with an empty scope
issueToken > refuses to issue a token that would already be expired
enforceToken > allows an action within scope on an active, unexpired token
enforceToken > logs every enforcement decision to the audit log
enforceToken > denies and logs an action outside the token's scope
enforceToken > denies an action once the token has expired
enforceToken > denies and logs an action against an unknown token id
AuditLog > returns a fresh array from entries() each call, not a live reference the caller could mutate
AuditLog > assigns each entry a unique id and the given occurredAt
stories.notes: Criterion 2 (revoked token blocked) is now genuinely true too — not from any test written for THIS story, but because STORY-002 (revokeToken + TokenStore) landed afterward and made it real; see revokeToken.test.ts. Flipped honestly rather than leaving it stale now that the underlying capability exists. issueToken and enforceToken both changed signature when STORY-002 introduced TokenStore as the source of truth (issueToken now takes a store and saves into it; enforceToken takes a token id and looks it up fresh, not a Token object) — this file's own tests were updated to match, all still passing.

criteria.text: Given a token, when it is revoked, then its next call fails immediately.
Given a revoked token, when it is used, then the action is blocked.
Trust: Revocation is logged with a reason code.

tests_added: revokeToken > makes the very next enforceToken call by id fail, right after revocation
revokeToken > blocks the action, not just reports a decision
revokeToken > logs the revocation itself with the given reason code
revokeToken > updates the token's own status to revoked in the store
revokeToken > refuses to revoke a token id that was never issued
stories.notes: Built a real TokenStore (in-memory Map, single source of truth by token id) rather than passing Token objects by value between calls, per explicit user direction that this build should demonstrate real, enterprise-grade behavior — not tests that pass by construction. enforceToken and revokeToken both re-read the store fresh on every call, so revocation is provably real-time: the proof in revokeToken.test.ts looks the token up by id again after revoking, never reuses the object issueToken originally returned. AuditLogEntry's decision union grew a third value ("revoked", alongside "allowed"/"denied") rather than starting a second log, per REQ-005's "one immutable audit log" framing. RevocationReason is a closed union (compromised/no_longer_needed/policy_violation/superseded), not a free-form string, since "logged with a reason code" implies a defined code, not arbitrary text.

criteria.text: Given a token request, when it is displayed, then the approver can approve or deny it.
Given a denied request, when it is submitted, then the token is not issued.
Trust: Approval actions are logged.

tests_added: requestToken > creates a pending request, not a token
approveRequest > issues a real token once an approver approves
approveRequest > logs the approval with the approver as actor
approveRequest > refuses to approve an unknown request id
approveRequest > refuses to approve the same request twice
denyRequest > does not issue a token when a request is denied
denyRequest > logs the denial with the approver, and a reason code when given
denyRequest > refuses to deny an unknown request id
denyRequest > refuses to deny an already-decided request
stories.notes: This is the story that actually closes the demo-path gap flagged at the end of STORY-002: added a real Express server (src/server.ts) and a Consent UI page (public/consent.html) — first genuinely interactive surface in the whole build, not just code+tests. Domain logic (RequestStore, requestToken/approveRequest/denyRequest) and the HTTP+UI layer were built as two separate confirmed steps. AuditLogEntry gained requestId/actor fields and request_approved/request_denied decision values; tokenId became optional since a denied request never gets one — verified via curl that a denied request's audit entry genuinely has no tokenId field at all. End-to-end verified over real HTTP, not mocked: submitted a request through the actual browser UI, approved it, confirmed a real token exists in the store, enforced an action against it (allowed), revoked it, confirmed the next enforcement is denied — then a separate request through the UI, denied via the Deny button, confirmed via the audit log that no token was ever created for it. Also smoke-tested error paths over HTTP directly (not just unit tests): double-approve → 409, unknown request id → 404, unknown token id on enforce → 200 with allowed:false (guardrail: deny, don't error, when validity can't be confirmed), missing required field → 400.

criteria.text: Given a subagent request, when it is processed, then it inherits a subset of the parent's scope.
Given a subagent request, when it exceeds the parent's scope, then it is denied.
Trust: Delegation actions are logged.

tests_added: delegateToken > issues a child token with a strict subset of the parent's scope
delegateToken > denies a request for scope the parent doesn't have
delegateToken > denies a request for the parent's exact scope, since that isn't narrower
delegateToken > denies an empty requested scope
delegateToken > denies delegation from an unknown parent token
delegateToken > denies delegation from a revoked parent token
delegateToken > denies delegation from an expired parent token
delegateToken > logs both an approved and a denied delegation attempt
delegateToken > caps a child token's expiry to the parent's, even if a longer TTL was requested
delegateToken > supports multi-level delegation — a subagent delegating to a sub-subagent
revokeToken cascading > revokes a delegated child when its parent is revoked
revokeToken cascading > cascades through multiple generations — a sub-subagent's token is revoked too
revokeToken cascading > logs each cascaded revocation with its own entry and a distinct reason code
stories.notes: REQ-003 says STRICT subset, taken literally: requesting the parent's exact scope back is denied (reasonCode 'not_narrower'), not treated as valid narrowing. User explicitly rejected leaving related real-world gaps for later ('i dont want any gaps... if that is a scenario that could happen in the real world then it needs to be done'), which expanded this story beyond the literal 3 acceptance criteria into two related invariants: (1) a delegated token's expiresAt is capped to its parent's, enforced inside issueToken() itself so it can't be bypassed by any future caller with a parentTokenId; (2) revokeToken() now cascades — revoking a token recursively revokes every descendant (TokenStore gained childrenOf()), each logged with reasonCode 'parent_revoked' to distinguish cascade-triggered revocations from human-chosen ones in the audit trail. Multi-level delegation (subagent delegating to a sub-subagent) falls out of the design for free — delegateToken() treats any active token as a valid parent, no special-casing needed. Added POST /tokens/:id/delegate to the HTTP API (returns 200 with approved:false on denial, same pattern as /enforce, since a refused delegation is a normal outcome not a fault) — kept the demo path consistent with every other capability in this build having a real interface, not just tests.

criteria.text: Given a valid token, when the token is used to access a mock endpoint, then the action is allowed.
Given an invalid token, when the token is used to access a mock endpoint, then the action is denied.
Trust: Given any token, when the token is used, then the action and its outcome are logged in the Audit Log.
Given a token request, when it is anomalous, then an alert is triggered.
Given a normal request, when it is processed, then no alert is triggered.
Trust: Anomaly detection actions are logged.

tests_added: AnomalyDetector > does not flag a single, reasonably-scoped request
AnomalyDetector > flags a request whose scope is unusually broad
AnomalyDetector > flags a burst of requests from the same subject within the window
AnomalyDetector > tracks velocity per subject, not globally
AnomalyDetector > does not count a request outside the velocity window
requestToken > does not log an anomaly alert for a normal request
requestToken > logs an anomaly alert for a request with unusually broad scope
requestToken > still creates the pending request even when it's flagged as anomalous
AnomalyDetector > honors a custom maxScopeBreadth instead of the default
AnomalyDetector > honors a custom maxRequestsPerWindow instead of the default
AnomalyDetector > falls back to the default for any config field left unset
stories.notes: Sequenced ahead of STORY-005 per the real dependency graph in plan.json (STORY-005.blocked_by includes STORY-006, not the reverse) — flagged the numbering mismatch to the user before starting rather than building 005 first and hitting the dependency out of order. Nothing in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md or docs/stories/STORY-006.md defines what 'anomalous' means, so picked two real, explainable, testable signals rather than a stub: scope breadth (>3 items in one request) and velocity (>3 requests from the same subject within a 60s window, tracked per-subject so one agent's burst can't flag an unrelated one — this is the concrete guard against the 'false positive alert is triggered' failure path named in the story). Wired into requestToken() itself (STORY-003) so every submission is checked automatically, not an opt-in step a caller could skip; only writes an audit entry when something actually fires, so 'no alert is triggered' for a normal request is literally true (checked as auditLog.entries() having length 0, not just an unasserted default) rather than a logged 'nothing found' entry every time. Detection is a signal only — an anomalous request still goes through the normal STORY-003 consent flow untouched, nothing here auto-denies it. User pushed back on an 85% confidence score being raised without anything actually changing ('i need the confidence score at 90'); rather than relabel the same number, made the underlying gap (thresholds as unconfirmed hardcoded judgment calls) real: AnomalyDetectorConfig is now constructor-injectable with a centralized DEFAULT_ANOMALY_CONFIG, and server.ts reads ANOMALY_MAX_SCOPE_BREADTH/ANOMALY_VELOCITY_WINDOW_MS/ANOMALY_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW env vars to override at runtime — a wrong guess is now a config change, not a code change. Verified live, not just unit-tested: started the server with ANOMALY_MAX_SCOPE_BREADTH=1 and confirmed a 2-item request was flagged that wouldn't be under the default.

criteria.text: Given a policy, when it is created, then it defines token scopes and constraints.
Given a policy, when it is modified, then changes are applied.
Trust: Policy actions are logged.
Given a developer, when they use the SDK, then they can request a token.
Given a token request, when it is invalid, then an error is returned.
Trust: SDK usage is logged.
Given the Policy & Token Store is unreachable, when a request is made, then it is denied.
Given the Store is reachable, when a request is made, then it is processed.
Trust: Circuit-breaker actions are logged.
Given a rejected token, when it is used, then a detailed error message is returned.
Given a valid token, when it is used, then no error message is returned.
Trust: Error message actions are logged.
Given a request for customer data, when the data is accessed, then sensitive fields are redacted.
Given a request for customer data, when the request lacks proper authorization, then access is denied.
Trust: Given any data access, when the data is accessed, then the access and redaction actions are logged in the Audit Log.
Given a denied action, when the action is logged, then a distinct reason code is recorded.
Given a denied action due to token expiration, when the action is logged, then the reason code indicates token expiration.
Trust: Given any denied action, when the action is logged, then the reason code is included in the Audit Log.
